title: 在训狗中学到的控制权与人性(3)
desc: 在训狗中学到的控制权与人性(3)

paragraphs.en: Many parents will be familiar with the name Penelope Leach, the psychologist and author of such books as Your Baby and Child.
paragraphs.zh: 很多家长都熟悉佩内洛普·利奇，这位心理学家写过《宝宝与孩子》这类著作。

paragraphs.en: Many dog owners will be equally familiar with the collected works of Steve Mann, including Easy Peasy Puppy Squeezy, Easy Peasy Doggy Squeezy, Easy Peasy Doggy Diary and Easy Peasy Awesome Pawsome.
paragraphs.zh: 很多养狗的人也同样熟悉史蒂夫·曼的全套作品，包括《超简单幼犬训练》《超简单家犬训练》《超简单狗狗日记》以及《超简单萌犬养成》。

paragraphs.en: Mann claims to have worked with more than 100,000 dogs worldwide, and has vicariously shaped the behaviour of many more, having founded the Institute of Modern Dog Training, which describes itself as the largest registered membership and accreditation body for dog trainers in the world.
paragraphs.zh: 曼声称，他在全球帮助过十万多只狗，还间接影响了更多犬只的行为。他创立了“现代犬只训练学会”，该机构自称是全球规模最大、拥有注册会员与认证体系的训犬师组织。

paragraphs.en: In addition to books, Mann produces podcasts and videos (including a "BBC Maestro" training course), while his minions crawl the Earth selling his behavioural wisdom.
paragraphs.zh: 除写书之外，曼还制作播客与视频，包括BBC大师课平台上的训犬课程，他的追随者遍布各地，传播他的行为学理念。

paragraphs.en: At various points over the past two years, I have scoured these books, watched the videos and paid hundreds of pounds to Steve Mann-accredited trainers, all in the desperate hope that some Mannite genius might finally solve the riddle of Dusty's undesirable, occasionally intolerable behaviours.
paragraphs.zh: 过去两年里，我反复研读这些书籍，观看教学视频，花数百英镑聘请曼体系认证的训犬师，绝望地希望某位曼学派高手，能破解达斯蒂那些令人头疼、有时难以忍受的行为难题。

paragraphs.en: Dog training is a lot about confidence and body language, and figures such as Mann possess a kind of aura, like a Pentecostal healer or an infant-sleep trainer, whereby the desperate layperson is willing to give up all autonomy, if only the guru will rescue them from their torments.
paragraphs.zh: 训犬很大程度关乎自信和肢体语言，曼这类人物自带一种气场，就像灵恩派疗愈师或是婴儿睡眠指导师。绝望的普通人愿意交出所有主见，只求这位大师能把自己从煎熬中解救出来。

paragraphs.en: The holy grail of dog training is focus, whereby the dog stares unerringly at their handler, waiting for instruction, regardless of distractions around them.
paragraphs.zh: 训犬的最高目标是专注力：无论周遭有什么干扰，狗狗目不转睛盯着训导员，等待指令。

paragraphs.en: The websites and YouTube videos of celebrity trainers feature images of smiling men and women sitting casually at picnic tables or standing in high streets while a seemingly hypnotised doberman or vizsla (never, I've noticed, a boxer …) stands stock still beside them – irrefutable evidence of the trainer's powers of control.
paragraphs.zh: 网红训犬师的网站和YouTube视频里，总能看到男女主人轻松坐在野餐桌旁，或是站在大街上，一只仿佛被催眠的杜宾或是维兹拉犬（我留意到，从来没有拳师犬……）一动不动站在身旁——无可辩驳地证明训犬师拥有强大的掌控力。

paragraphs.en: Like an Instagram financial influencer leaning on his Ferrari, the message is: if I did this, you can too.
paragraphs.zh: 就像社交平台上的理财博主靠在法拉利旁拍照，传递的信息是：我能做到，你也可以。

paragraphs.en: But how?
paragraphs.zh: 但到底要怎么做？

paragraphs.en: Over recent decades, Mann has been at the forefront of a revolution in dog training that contradicts assumptions about discipline and ethics elsewhere in our lives.
paragraphs.zh: 近几十年来，曼一直走在训犬变革的前沿，这套理念和我们生活里其他领域的惩戒、伦理观念相悖。

paragraphs.en: His guiding principle is that of behaviourism, an approach to the control and prediction of human and non-human activity that deliberately discards all moral language in favour of rewards.
paragraphs.zh: 他的核心理论是行为主义，这套方法用来管控、预测人类与非人类生物的行为，刻意摒弃所有道德话语，转而依靠奖励机制。

paragraphs.en: As the American psychologist BF Skinner, the high priest of behaviourism, argued in the 1950s and 60s, people and animals are fundamentally alike: what they do is a consequence of their immediate environment and past experiences, rather than of values or intentions.
paragraphs.zh: 行为主义的代表人物，美国心理学家B.F.斯金纳在二十世纪五六十年代提出，人与动物本质上是一样的：他们的行为，是当下环境与过往经历带来的结果，而非价值观或是主观意图。

paragraphs.en: Any behaviour can be explained (and thereby controlled) as a response to a stimulus of some kind.
paragraphs.zh: 任何行为，都可以被解读为对某种刺激做出的反应，也因此可以被管控。

paragraphs.en: The starting point of Mann's approach is that dogs have suffered over centuries by having their behaviour described in moralising human language.
paragraphs.zh: 曼这套方法的出发点是：几百年来，人们用带有道德评判色彩的人类语言描述狗狗的行为，让犬只蒙受误解。

paragraphs.en: When dog owners call their pets "bad" or "naughty" – or say that "she's ignoring me on purpose" or "looking guilty" – they are gearing themselves up to deliver the most obvious response: punishment.
paragraphs.zh: 当主人说自家宠物“坏”、“淘气”，或是说“它故意不理我”“露出愧疚的神情”，这时人们已经准备好采取最直接的手段：惩罚。

paragraphs.en: The standard way to get a dog under control, through most of the history of human-canine relations, has been to restrain or hit it, often with a shout of "bad dog!"
paragraphs.zh: 在人与犬相伴的漫长历史里，控制狗狗最常规的方式，就是束缚或是殴打，常常伴随着一声呵斥：坏狗！

paragraphs.en: On first encountering dog trainers shouting and yanking on leads, Mann wondered: "Why don't we just focus on what we do want, rather than only looking for the 'bad'?"
paragraphs.zh: 曼最早看到训犬师大喊大叫、猛拽牵引绳时，心生疑问：“为什么我们不去关注希望看到的行为，而不是一味盯着‘错误’？”

paragraphs.en: This is the insight that became the basis of "positive reinforcement" methods: every time your dog does something you want it to do, you reward it with food as quickly as possible.
paragraphs.zh: 这个想法催生了“正向强化”训练法：每当狗狗做出你想要的行为，尽快用食物奖励它。

paragraphs.en: If the reward is high enough (and, crucially, quick enough), your dog will obey you, and from there you simply have to reinforce the behaviour through repetition.
paragraphs.zh: 只要奖励足够诱人（关键是奖励要及时），狗狗就会服从你，之后你只需要不断重复，巩固这种行为。

paragraphs.en: Your dog is never "ignoring" you or "doing it on purpose", because – as Skinner might have observed – they don't do anything on purpose: they just respond to cues.
paragraphs.zh: 狗狗从来不是“故意无视”或者“存心捣乱”，正如斯金纳可能会说的那样：它们不会带着主观目的做事，只是对信号做出反应。

paragraphs.en: The term "reactive" has become the modern catch-all term for any dog that behaves aggressively (usually interpreted as a symptom of fear), another attempt to cleanse dog training of anthropocentric language.
paragraphs.zh: “反应过激”已经成了现代通用术语，用来形容任何表现出攻击性的狗（通常被解读为恐惧的表现），这又是一次尝试，把拟人化的语言从训犬领域剔除。

paragraphs.en: As I navigated this literature, I began to recognise elements of a more infamous critique of morality – the one, surprising as it may sound, found in the work of Friedrich Nietzsche.
paragraphs.zh: 研读这些文献的时候，我发现其中一些观点，和弗里德里希·尼采那套饱受争议的道德批判有着惊人的相似之处。

paragraphs.en: Moralising and punishing don't work for dogs, modern trainers argue, for the same reason that they do work for humans, according to Nietzsche.
paragraphs.zh: 现代训犬师提出，道德评判与惩罚对狗不起作用。而按照尼采的理论，这套手段之所以能作用于人类，自有其原因。

paragraphs.en: If a dog breaks a rule and then gets punished two minutes later, it has no understanding of how one led to the other.
paragraphs.zh: 如果狗狗违反规则，两分钟之后才受到惩罚，它完全无法理解两件事之间的因果关联。

paragraphs.en: All it knows is that it has been harmed.
paragraphs.zh: 它只会知道自己受到了伤害。

paragraphs.en: For Nietzsche, humans become moral creatures once they understand how transgression A leads to penalty B, even when there is a substantial delay – potentially years – between the two.
paragraphs.zh: 尼采认为，人类之所以成为有道德的生物，是因为能够理解，行为A会招致惩罚B，哪怕两件事相隔很久，甚至时隔数年。

paragraphs.en: Humans are disciplined, punished and educated until they acquire that internal capacity that Nietzsche believed was most repressive of all: a guilty conscience, the most ingenious instrument of control ever invented.
paragraphs.zh: 人类在规训、惩罚与教育中，慢慢形成一种内在心理，尼采认为这是所有压抑中最甚的东西：愧疚之心，人类发明的最精妙的控制工具。

paragraphs.en: Freedom from guilt would mean living in the moment and forgetting one's sins: in other words, becoming more like dogs.
paragraphs.zh: 摆脱愧疚，意味着活在当下，遗忘过错；换句话说，变得更像狗。

paragraphs.en: To what extent is "positive reinforcement" a viable alternative to morality and guilt?
paragraphs.zh: “正向强化”究竟能在多大程度上替代道德与愧疚？

paragraphs.en: It seems very simple on paper, until you have to incorporate it into your everyday life.
paragraphs.zh: 在书上看看似乎很简单，但只有把这套方法融入日常的时候才发现有多难。

paragraphs.en: If a dog can't be held accountable for its actions, then the finger of suspicion turns towards its entire environment instead: maybe it's the wrong treats, the wrong harness, the wrong time of day to be walking, the wrong owner.
paragraphs.zh: 既然无法让动物为自身行为负责，怀疑的目光就会转向它所处的整个环境：或许是零食选错了，胸背带不合适，遛狗时间不对，主人本身不合格。

paragraphs.en: I even know of a case of a couple moving house, because they became convinced that this was the key to improving their dog's behaviour.
paragraphs.zh: 我甚至听说一对夫妻搬了家，因为他们坚信，搬家是改善狗狗行为的关键。

paragraphs.en: There is a darker side to the behaviourist worldview, the one explored in the gruelling experiments undertaken on the ethically abhorrent protagonist of A Clockwork Orange.
paragraphs.zh: 行为主义世界观还有阴暗的一面，《发条橙》里那个饱受残酷实验、伦理上饱受诟病的主角，就展现了这一点。

paragraphs.en: If an animal doesn't have the capacity to connect behaviour and punishment when there is a delay between the two, what happens if you eliminate the delay?
paragraphs.zh: 如果动物无法在行为和延迟的惩罚之间建立关联，那倘若消除这个时间差，又会发生什么？

paragraphs.en: I've sometimes wondered how my grandmother could possibly have handled a boxer, but then remember that Folly wore a choke collar.
paragraphs.zh: 我有时会好奇祖母当年是怎么养好拳师犬的，随即想起福利戴过窒息项圈。

paragraphs.en: If my gran pulled on the lead, a chain tightened around her neck.
paragraphs.zh: 祖母一拽牵引绳，铁链就会收紧勒住它的脖子。

paragraphs.en: Remote control electric shock collars expand the reach of punitive conditioning.
paragraphs.zh: 遥控电击项圈，进一步拓展了惩罚式条件反射训练的边界。

paragraphs.en: The ethics and effectiveness of these collars is a matter of heated controversy, and legislation was introduced under the last Conservative government to ban them in England (Wales is the only place in the UK where they are banned), but never made its way through parliament.
paragraphs.zh: 这类项圈的伦理争议巨大，效果也饱受质疑。上一届保守党政府曾提出立法，打算在英格兰禁止电击项圈（威尔士是英国唯一已经禁掉该设备的地区），但法案最终没能在议会通过。

paragraphs.en: I would never use an electric shock collar or choke collar, and understand the futility of punishing Dusty for deeds that she's long forgotten about.
paragraphs.zh: 我绝不会使用电击项圈或是窒息项圈，也明白惩罚早已忘记事情的达斯蒂毫无意义。

paragraphs.en: My commitment to "positive reinforcement" is pretty unwavering.
paragraphs.zh: 我坚定地坚持“正向强化”原则。

paragraphs.en: I even try to avoid shouting "no!", which Steve Mann assures me doesn't work on a dog.
paragraphs.zh: 我甚至尽量不喊“不行！”，史蒂夫·曼向我保证，这句话对狗起不到作用。

paragraphs.en: But when nothing seems to be working, I have fantasised about doing some far worse things, and never more so than when Dusty hit the so-called "teenage" phase.
paragraphs.zh: 但当所有办法都收效甚微时，我脑海里闪过更极端的念头，达斯蒂进入所谓“青春期”的时候尤甚。
